finding.claim: purge() calls checkPerm() but discards the boolean result, so the admin check is never enforced. Any authenticated user, including one with no admin permission, can run purgeAll(). This is a broken authorization / missing enforcement bug. rotateKeys() uses mustPerm correctly, which shows the intended pattern.
finding.source: Any authenticated HTTP request to the purge handler. The user need not hold the 'admin' permission.
finding.sink: purgeAll() at handlers.go:27, a destructive admin-only operation.

trace.note: u := userFrom(r) loads the caller's user from the request context
checkPerm(u, "admin") returns false for a non-admin, but the result is ignored and there is no early return

finding.guards_checked: checkPerm has no side effects: it does not write a 403 and does not abort. No other check exists in purge(). The calling middleware and route registration are not in this directory, so I could not confirm whether an outer admin guard exists. rotateKeys is correctly guarded by mustPerm at line 33. userFrom (line 40) does an unchecked type assertion, which panics if there is no user in the context. That is a robustness issue, not an authorization bypass.

verdict.guard_found: none in purge(); checkPerm (handlers.go:12) returns a bool with no side effects and its result is discarded at line 26. The outer middleware and routing are not in the directory.
verdict.reason: At handlers.go:26 the bool from checkPerm(u, "admin") is discarded, so purgeAll() at line 27 runs for any authenticated user, unlike rotateKeys, which tests mustPerm at handlers.go:33. An outer middleware guard could exist, but nothing in this directory shows one.
